behavior: The public Cloudflare record is destroyed and the name no longer resolves
evidence: 2026-08-09: `make tf-dns-plan` reported `Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy`, the single resource being cloudflare_record.kubelab_svc["ollama"] (A, ollama.kubelab.live -> 162.55.57.175, proxied=false, id b5a3dc58a24db92a83c1ed81c0f00c73). Terraform's stated reason is `because key ["ollama"] is not in for_each map` — the record was removed by shrinking the desired set in services.json (#915), which is why merging that PR was inert until the apply. Applied: outputs went kubelab_record_count 16 -> 15 and the ollama entry left kubelab_service_urls. Verified after: `dig +short ollama.kubelab.live @1.1.1.1` empty, and empty at the authoritative NS too, while api.kubelab.live still resolves (104.21.56.20 / 172.67.175.250) — so the zone was not damaged.

behavior: The out-of-band Middleware is gone from the LIVE prod cluster - the object Argo never tracked, so a git-only check cannot see it. NOTE: there is no backing Secret and there never was; the API key is inline in the Middleware spec (keys: [${API_KEY}] in api-key.yaml.tpl). The secret clause below is kept as a guard against a future variant, not because one existed
verification: ! kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/kubelab-prod-config get middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab 2>/dev/null && ! kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/kubelab-prod-config get secret -n kubelab -o name 2>/dev/null | grep -qi ollama
evidence: 2026-08-09: before deletion `kubectl get middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab` returned it at AGE 78d, and `get secret -n kubelab -o name | grep -i ollama` was already empty — confirming no Secret ever backed it. Deleted with a supervised one-off (`kubectl delete middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab`, authorized by Manu) because the toolkit has an apply path and no delete path; filed as its own gap. Post-check: both clauses pass. The two remaining ollama middlewares, ollama-inflight and ollama-ratelimit, are git-tracked in overlays/prod/ollama-throttle.yaml and are Argo's to prune on PR-B merge, not this probe's concern. Edge smoke after deletion: api.kubelab.live 200, auth.kubelab.live 200 — removing a middleware referenced by a soon-to-be-pruned IngressRoute did not affect other routers. Deleting it also removed a plaintext prod API key from etcd, since the key is inline in the Middleware spec rather than in a Secret.
